finding: TI UCC27282DRCR VSON-10 has an integrated bootstrap diode; current BOM also has D_BT. Existence/function of a separate diode must be reconciled against actual native schematic; no automatic deletion.
action: Draw internal diode and any external D_BT on the same electrical net schematic; determine purpose/OR-ing, loop, reverse stress and errata; update actual EDA only after review
progress: The vendored datasheet resolves the duplicate question without deleting anything: references/datasheets/ucc27282.txt Table 5-1 puts HB on DRC pin 3 (pin 2 is NC) and says 'the bootstrap diode is on-chip', adding 'when using external boot diode, connect cathode of the diode to this pin'. The native netlist has U2.3=HB and D_BT pin 1 (cathode) on HB, anode on VCC12, so the external diode is a datasheet-sanctioned parallel path, not a wiring error. What remains open is whether to populate it and with what part: when QH is on the external diode holds off HB-VCC12 = 48 V, so the 30 V BAT54WS placeholder cannot be used; the BOM's >=100 V requirement stands. The reverse stress is now measured rather than only computed: with the model's Cbt held at 12 V, the external diode's reverse voltage is V(hb) - V(aux) = V(sw), and over the complete 320 us hotfault records V(sw) peaks at 49.10 V on the 48 V srprobe raw (minimum -1.44 V) and 51.13 V on the 50 V cshunt srprobe raw (minimum -1.50 V), i.e. 1.02x the input rail. That is a lower bound on the real part stress, not an upper one: the behavioural switch has no package inductance, so no V = L*di/dt overshoot appears on the edge. The >=100 V BOM requirement therefore keeps about 2x margin against the modelled peak only. Native GUI review of loop and reverse stress is still missing.

finding: TI CSD19531Q5A: 5.3 mOhm at 10V is typical, 6.4 mOhm is maximum. Existing BOM wording 6.2 mOhm max conflicts with current TI product page. Power-stage loss stress must use a relevant maximum and hot-temperature Rds(on).
action: Reconcile manufacturer datasheet Rev.B and original BOM; quantify max-temperature conduction/switching loss; do not auto-upgrade verified_mpn
progress: The vendored Rev.B text already carries the 6.4 mOhm max (RDS(on) table, VGS=10 V, ID=16 A); the 6.2 in the BOM was not traceable to it. design/v3/bom/bom_draft.csv now says 6.4 max and tools/test_bom_draft.py re-reads the vendored table so the number cannot drift. Figure 8 gives normalised on-resistance about 1.55 at 125 C (typical) and 1.78 at 150 C, so a hot-case typical is ~9.9 / ~11.4 mOhm; the datasheet publishes no max-over-temperature curve, so these are not guaranteed maxima. Scaling the 48 V/120 A ledger's measured I^2R terms (sh 0.5502 W + sl 0.5489 W at the deck's 8 mOhm lump) gives +0.261 W at 9.9 mOhm and +0.467 W at 11.4 mOhm, i.e. about -0.11 / -0.19 percentage points of the 94.23 % port efficiency at fixed waveforms. Switching loss is untouched by this datum; the junction-temperature and gate-loop parts of the action remain open. The remaining junction-temperature half cannot be taken from the deck's own primary-current traces: the 48 V/120 A hotfault raw saves |I(SH)| peaking at 776.8 A and |I(SL)| at 750.7 A, but each peak is nine samples spanning 0.08 ns (two solver steps) and recurs once per half cycle (168.6209 / 173.6062 us). At the peak instant I(Lr) is only 0.31 A and V(sw) is 26.73 V, so the current is the 1.12 nF of Cdh+Cdl being charged through the 8 mOhm behavioural switch - a lumped-capacitance edge with no package inductance to limit di/dt, not a drain current a real device would carry. The time-weighted I^2R over the pre-fault decade is 0.5546 W (sh) / 0.5476 W (sl), which reproduces the published 100 A ledger's 0.5502/0.5489 W, so the spikes carry no energy; averaging by sample count instead of by time gives 2.697 W, 4.9x too high, because LTspice packs samples into the edge. The vendored CSD19531Q5A PDF does contain SOA (page indices 1 and 5) and transient thermal impedance (index 3), but its vector layout is unlike the BSC010N04LS6 chart (1.469 pt curve strokes, plain-number 6.9 pt ticks) and it prints no SOA value that could anchor a digitisation, so the method used for SOURCE-03 cannot be transplanted without an independent calibration. Screening the primary switches needs a device-level model with package inductance and Coss, not this ideal SW element.

finding: Infineon BSC010N04LS6 max Rds(on) 1.0 mOhm @10V; 285A case-limited continuous and 1140A pulse figures do NOT establish fault SOA at measured Vds, pulse shape, width or Tj.
action: Use complete 2022 Rev.2.3 original SOA and transient Zth with explicit current and Vds waveforms; verify 8 SRs and gate shutdown
progress: The vendored BSC010N04LS6 PDF (references/datasheets/bsc010n04ls6.pdf, sha256 c868cf67...) is now digitised rather than quoted: tools/vendor_soa.py recovers the six SOA curves and the single-pulse transient-impedance trace from page 6, and design/v3/power_priority/vendor_soa_digitized.json records the axis calibration with its own error. Three anchors hold it: the 1 us plateau digitises to 1125 A against the 1140 A printed in the same document (-1.3 %), the drawn right edge lands at 41.07 V on a 40 V rated device (+2.7 %), and the Zth trace reaches 0.994 K/W at 1 s against a 1 K/W Rth(j-c). The screen (tools/sr_soa_screen.py, design/v3/power_priority/sr_soa_screen.json) runs over all eight SRs in three fault-deck runs. First quadrant: every sample of every device is compared point by point with the 10 us and 100 us curves, and the worst utilisation is 6.30 % (48 V), 6.33 % (48 V cshunt), 6.52 % (50 V cshunt) - the blocking and reverse-recovery excursions are an order of magnitude inside the chart. Third quadrant: this is where the fault actually lives and the vendor diagram does not draw it, so no curve governs it; the record states the measured stress instead - -292.61 A / 15.54 V on 48 V and -303.50 A / 15.46 V on 50 V cshunt, with a package-level product of 351-374 W that includes the lead inductance. Thermal: the die probes (pair 1 only) give a peak die dissipation of 190.7 W (48 V) and 214.2 W (50 V cshunt) over a 4.5-4.7 us energy-equivalent width, and convolution with the digitised Zth lifts Tj by 1.84-1.88 K from a 3.0-4.3 W pre-fault state - far from the 175 C limit, but this is a simulated waveform, not a rating. Gate shutdown: the srprobe records show the post-trip latch is 1.2-1.4 A and about 1e-4 A^2s per device, i.e. a low-current latch rather than large-current conduction, in one or the other phase depending on the solver path. Table 7 of the vendored datasheet settles where those two numbers come from and shows they are not a matched pair: the 285 A is ID, the first-quadrant continuous drain rating at TC=25 C, while the reverse-diode row gives IS = 150 A continuous and IS,pulse = 1140 A at TC=25 C with no pulse width stated. Pairing 285 A with 1140 A therefore mixes two terminals, and neither describes the measured third-quadrant 13 us conduction. A separate behavioural protection candidate (design/v3/power_priority/PROT02_独立故障锁存候选对照_2026-11-03.md sections 4.3 and 5.3) does drive all eight SR gates low for the rest of the 320 us window at both 48 V and 50 V, cutting the eight-device forward I^2t by about 95 %, but its clamp is an ideal 0.05 ohm switch and its latch an ideal behavioural block, so it is a candidate for the gate-shutdown half, not a hardware shutdown circuit. STILL OPEN: the model pins TJ at 25 C with no thermal feedback and has no vendor SOA for VDS < 0, so the third-quadrant stress has no acceptance criterion; the UCC24624 standby/light-load shutdown is not modelled, so the latch in the unprotected deck cannot be called a safe gate shutdown; and the 285 A / 1140 A figures remain marketing context, not the basis of this screen.

finding: Panasonic 0805 10ohm ERJ6ENF10R0V is nominally 0.125W, but the measured continuous burden dissipation is 125.7mW at 48V/120A (mean(V^2)/R), already 100.6% of the nominal rating before any temperature de-rating; the fault pulse peaks at 9.36-10.08W with an equivalent width of about 13us.
action: Select a larger or pulse-rated 10 ohm part; obtain the vendor pulse-derating curve and local-ambient temperature; confirm the derived startup pulse with a raw that saves the burden nodes before closing the package decision
progress: P_rated is now taken from V(ocd)-V(ocm) across the deck's own Rbur=10 ohm in the srprobe raws (tools/oc_burden_pulse.py, design/v3/bom/oc_burden_pulse.json). The earlier 69.6mW/103mW figures used mean(V)^2/R, which is low by the rectified waveform's form factor squared (1.102 here): the correct continuous value is 125.7mW at 48V/120A, i.e. already at 100.6% of the 0.125W nominal before the 70C-to-155C linear de-rating. The fault pulse, previously called unmeasured because no raw saved V(ocd), is measurable now that the srprobe family saves it: peak 9.359W (48V) / 10.072-10.083W (50V), energy 0.1226/0.1309mJ, equivalent width 13.1us; PROT-B reduces it to 2.07W / 0.0060mJ. No Panasonic pulse-derating curve is vendored, so the pulse is a selection input, not a pass/fail. The 8ms cold-start deck does not save the burden nodes, so the startup pulse is not measured directly; it is derived from the saved I(Lr) through the deck's own ideal transformer (V_burden = Rbur*|i_pri|/N, Rbur=10 ohm, N=sqrt(20mH/2uH)=100), with the transfer calibrated on the hotfault srprobe raw over 2-97 A (median 0.0997355 V/A, p05-p95 0.0993-0.1023, spread about 3% of the median; nominal 0.1 V/A). That transfer reproduces the independently measured steady 7-8ms burden (0.1253W derived vs 0.1257W measured, 0.319% apart), which is the check that the derivation is not self-fulfilling. Cold start: peak 0.579361W at 1.28698ms (|I(Lr)| 24.1338A, Vout 1.1664V), energy 0.778649mJ over 8ms (mean 97.33mW), of which the first 2ms carries 0.0944709mJ (12.1%). Against the 1.5W 2512 candidate the startup peak is 0.386x P70 with 0us above P70, and 1.094x/2.189x/6.566x the 125/140/150C de-rated values, staying above them for 0.431/11.02/4071us; those are screening ratios from a 10ns-max-step deck, not pass/fail. The startup carries 6.35x the fault pulse's total energy (0.7786 vs 0.1226mJ) at 1/16 its peak, so the package decision is now set by startup energy rather than by the fault pulse. Source: design/v3/bom/startup_burden_pulse.json (tools/startup_burden_pulse.py). Direct confirmation is still a cold-start raw that saves V(ocd)/V(ocm). As-of 2026-11-03: rejected 0805 ERJ6ENF10R0V in active candidate mapping; proposed Vishay CRCW251210R0FKEHHP 10Ω 1% 1.5W 2512 (official CRCW-HP e3 Rev 17-Mar-2026; exact order code confirmed on DigiKey). P70 / max pre-fault model power = 11.93x (not a derated hardware value). Vishay p5 has single/repetitive pulse charts, but waveform-equivalent width alone does not certify nonrectangular pulse; real board temperature still missing and the startup waveform is derived rather than measured.
